titleStmt.title: Draft Declaration on the Italian Peace Treaty

head.hi: Draft Declaration on the Italian Peace Treaty

div.p: His Majesty’s Government in the United Kingdom have for some time been considering how best to resolve, in the interests of the peaceful development of Western Europe, in particular, and of the free nations as a whole, the problem presented by the Peace Treaty with Italy, a co-belligerent at the conclusion of the last war.

2. An anomaly results from the fact that, although Italy has taken her rightful place among the free nations as a member of the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, she is still prevented from membership of the United Nations and is still bound by the terms of the Treaty of Peace of February, 1947, certain clauses of which may prove inconsistent with her legitimate right of self-defence.

3. His Majesty’s Government are considering what proposals they can make with a view to removing this anomaly. But, so long as the present position prevails, His Majesty’s Government make the following declaration:—

(1) So far as they are concerned, His Majesty’s Government will be governed in their general relations with Italy, henceforward, by the spirit of the Atlantic Alliance rather than by that of the Peace Treaty.
(2) His Majesty’s Government continue to favour the admission of Italy to the United Nations.
(3) His Majesty’s Government recognize to the Italian Government, in principle, the legitimate right of self-defence.
